target.rawSql: SELECT period_start AS time, 'anomaly' AS text, CASE WHEN forest_flagged THEN 'forest' ELSE 'flatline' END AS tags FROM eia_anomalies WHERE reading_type='D' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND $__timeFilter(period_start)

targets.rawSql: SELECT value_mw * 1000000 AS value FROM eia_readings WHERE respondent='PJM' AND reading_type='D' AND quality != 'missing' ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT max(value_mw) * 1000000 AS value FROM eia_readings WHERE respondent='PJM' AND reading_type='D' AND period_start > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: Data freshness
panels.description: Time since the most recent EIA demand reading. EIA-930 is hourly, so a healthy value here is well under 2 hours.

targets.rawSql: SELECT extract(epoch from (now() - max(period_start))) AS value FROM eia_readings WHERE respondent='PJM' AND reading_type='D'
SELECT count(*) AS value FROM eia_anomalies WHERE reading_type='D' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND scored_at > now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: Demand vs forecast
panels.description: The project's single money panel. Forecast is the seasonal-naive baseline the detector actually scores against (model/baselines.py), derived here as actual - residual, not a separately stored column. Flagged intervals are marked as annotations.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.period_start AS time, r.value_mw * 1000000 AS actual, (r.value_mw - a.residual) * 1000000 AS forecast FROM eia_readings r LEFT JOIN eia_anomalies a ON a.period_start = r.period_start AND a.reading_type = r.reading_type WHERE r.respondent='PJM' AND r.reading_type='D' AND $__timeFilter(r.period_start) ORDER BY r.period_start

panels.title: Forecast residuals
panels.description: The series the isolation forest actually scores. Flagged points (forest-flagged) are shown as a separate overlaid series so you can see why something was flagged, not just that it was.

targets.rawSql: SELECT period_start AS time, residual * 1000000 AS residual, CASE WHEN forest_flagged THEN residual * 1000000 ELSE NULL END AS flagged FROM eia_anomalies WHERE reading_type='D' AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start

SELECT period_start AS "Time", residual * 1000000 AS "Residual (W)", forest_score AS "Forest score", forest_flagged AS "Forest flagged", flatline_flagged AS "Flatline flagged", scored_at AS "Scored at" FROM eia_anomalies WHERE reading_type='D' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 100

panels.title: Net generation and total interchange
panels.description: Context, not detection. EIA-930 reports a single aggregate net-generation figure, not a fuel-type breakdown, so this is not a generation mix panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT period_start AS time, value_mw * 1000000 AS net_generation FROM eia_readings WHERE respondent='PJM' AND reading_type='NG' AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start
SELECT period_start AS time, value_mw * 1000000 AS total_interchange FROM eia_readings WHERE respondent='PJM' AND reading_type='TI' AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start

options.content: **How this detector works.** An isolation forest scores the residual (actual minus a seasonal-naive forecast) plus rolling context features, fit only on data through mid-2025 and calibrated on a later validation window it never trained on, same time-based split used throughout this project to avoid lookahead leakage. A separate rule-based check independently flags sustained flatlines (a failure mode an anomaly-on-residual model alone does not reliably catch). **There are no real anomaly labels for this data.** Detector quality is instead measured by injecting synthetic anomalies (spikes, step changes, flatlines, abnormal ramps) into held-out data and measuring recall at a fixed false-positive budget, a check on the method, not a guarantee about real events. See the project's ARCHITECTURE.md for the full methodology and the real recall numbers this was measured at.
